## Custom Electrochemical Flow Cell

I developed an in-house flow-cell platform using a design-to-test workflow:

**SolidWorks CAD → resin additive manufacturing → Nomad CNC / graphite machining → assembly → electrochemical testing**

The platform supports controlled studies of suspension-electrode transport and electrochemical performance.

## Taylor–Couette Electrochemical Platform

Designed a customized Taylor–Couette configuration for controlled suspension-flow and transport measurements, with emphasis on separating hydrodynamic and electrochemical effects.

## Yield-Stress Rotating-Flow Modeling

Developed reduced-order numerical models and finite-element simulations for rotating Newtonian, Bingham, and Herschel–Bulkley flows.

Key computational elements include:

- nonlinear boundary-value solvers
- continuation methods
- similarity and scaling analysis
- finite-geometry COMSOL models
- yielded / unyielded region analysis
- systematic comparison with prior literature

## Coupled Fluid–Particle Heat Transfer

Built an ANSYS Fluent + Discrete Phase Method model for heat and momentum transfer in a serpentine microtube. The model examined single-phase and dilute particle-laden cases, including two-way momentum and energy coupling.

**Topics:** CFD, DPM, laminar/turbulent transport, particle trajectories, heat transfer, mesh comparison.

## Corrosion Under Insulation Modeling

Developed COMSOL finite-element models for oxygen transport and corrosion in thin electrolyte films relevant to corrosion-under-insulation environments.

**Topics:** diffusion, electrochemical transport, multiphysics coupling, thin-film modeling.

## Research Infrastructure

As the first PhD student in a newly established research group, I have also contributed to building the research environment itself:

- equipment procurement and commissioning
- laboratory safety and operating procedures
- instrument maintenance and vendor support
- custom experimental setup development
- undergraduate research mentoring

This operational experience is an important part of how I approach research engineering: a model or experiment is useful only if it can be implemented, validated, and maintained.
